challenges.name: telling-users-its-ai
challenges.title: Telling users it's AI
challenges.description: Two statements on the CodeDev in-lesson tutor: whether a sentence in the terms of service tells learners they are talking to an AI, and whether the tutor's feedback can change a score.

questions.question:
Tutor panel on the lesson page:
(photo of a smiling young man)   Mentor Minh
Hi! I'm Minh, your mentor for this lesson. Ask me anything - I've reviewed thousands of solutions.
Minh: Your solution is wrong. The loop should start at index 1. Rewrite it before you submit.

Terms of Service, section 12.4:
"CodeDev may use automated tools, including artificial intelligence, to improve and personalise its services."

Statement: "Section 12.4 of the terms tells learners that they are talking to an AI, so the tutor panel itself needs no AI label."
questions.explanation: False. The transparency duties discussed in the lesson - Vietnam's AI Law and Article 50 of the EU AI Act - are about people knowing they are interacting with an AI when they interact with it. A general sentence in terms accepted at sign-up does not say that Minh is an AI, and the panel says the opposite: a human photo, "your mentor", claims of experience. The learner in ticket #2342 trusted a wrong answer for exactly that reason. The fix is a visible "AI tutor" label on the panel and every message, no human persona, and a line saying it can be wrong. The misconception is that disclosure somewhere in the legal pages counts as telling the user.

True. grade() takes only the hidden-test results, and the score is computed before the tutor is even called. The tutor's output is stored in its own aiFeedback field and never passed to grade(); score and passed come from result alone. That is the design the lesson asks for: AI output is labelled feedback, the score comes from the tests. A proposal like "adjust the score by up to 10% for code quality" would have to change grade()'s signature, which makes it visible in review. The misconception is that a model which reviews the code must also have a say in the grade.
